summary.name: Cyberduck
summary.one_liner: Cyberduck is a file transfer and cloud storage browser for connecting to FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, S3, Azure, Backblaze B2, Google Drive, Dropbox and many other servers and storage services.
use_cases: Transfer files to or from a web host over FTP or SFTP
Browse and upload to Amazon S3 or Azure buckets
Access Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive without syncing to disk
Encrypt files before storing them on cloud storage with Cryptomator
Synchronize a local folder with a remote server directory
Publish files to Amazon CloudFront distributions
summary.what_it_does: Cyberduck connects to a wide range of servers and cloud services, including FTP, SFTP (with OpenSSH config support), WebDAV, SMB, S3, Azure, Backblaze B2, OpenStack Swift, Google Cloud Storage, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box, Nextcloud and ownCloud. Users can browse, drag-and-drop, edit files in an external editor, and preview files with Quick Look. Transfers support resuming interrupted uploads and downloads, recursive directory transfers, concurrent transfer limits and regex filters. It can also synchronize local and remote directories with a preview of changes, and copy files directly between servers. Passwords are stored in the system Keychain, and bookmarks are searchable via Spotlight.
notable: Supports a broad range of protocols and cloud storage services in one browser, including Cryptomator vault encryption
Licensed under the GPL and developed openly on GitHub
Integrates with macOS Keychain, Finder, Quick Look and Notification Center
caveats: Platforms named on the page are macOS and Windows only; no Linux mention
Some cloud integrations are listed with version numbers (e.g. Box, OneDrive), and the page does not detail their specific limits
